question: with several slots, can one running conversation cost and compute exactly what it does on a single slot - MTP included - if every conversation keeps its own run of the KV pool; and what was the intermittent "bad allocation"
setup: production profile with image input off, 4 slots over one 262144-cell pool. The release build and 0.1.10 each run from a bundle (dist/runtime, and a copy of 0.1.10's), so both load the SDK's HIP runtime - see "runtime" below - interleaved in one session. tmp/pool_probe.py puts 50163 + 18939 + 1285 tokens of idle conversations in slots 1-3, then decodes 256 greedy tokens on a 23052-token conversation in slot 0; tmp/kvr/final_runs.py and final_runs_d.py hold the exact runs

design.layout: every conversation keeps one run of cells, in slot order. Its tokens go after its last cell; a new one starts after the last conversation, leaving the one before it LLAMA_KV_REGION_HEADROOM cells (8192) or half of what is left, on a 256-cell boundary
design.rebalance: a batch that does not fit after its conversations has the pool laid out again first (plan_layout): the conversations keep their order and slide towards the start or the end; each one of the batch gets the same room after it (the headroom, or an equal share of the free cells when that is less), an idle one none, a new one goes last. Moves towards the start run first, lowest first, then those towards the end, highest first, and a conversation that moves by less than its own length goes in pieces no longer than the distance, so no copy overwrites a cell still to be copied. Shared cells, interleaved conversations or a full pool leave the pool as it is, and the tokens take the old search, which is correct and only widens the window
design.moves: device-to-device copies of every layer's K/V rows, the indexer keys and the block keys, queued in init_batch on the stream the graphs run on, so nothing waits on the host; the cells' bookkeeping moves a run at a time (llama_kv_cells::mv_range, which took a 70K-cell rebalance from ~120 to ~45 ms of host time). A restore that finds no run large enough lays the pool out the same way first and waits for the copies, since it writes cells next
design.window: the graph of a batch views [first cell, last cell] of its own conversations, padded as before, instead of the pool from cell 0; every cell index in the mask and the sparse-attention inputs is relative to it, the block-key rows stay absolute; a graph is reused only for the same first cell
design.block keys: go stale per sequence (restore, shift, a move that reorders cells) instead of per pool; the next graph of that sequence rebuilds its own keys inside its window

memory.the limit: commit limit 127.6 GB (31.6 GB of RAM + a 96 GB page file); about 25 GB of it is the system's. Device allocations of ~3.5 GB and up count against it one for one, smaller ones did not (tmp/kvr/hipfill_test.py, hiprealloc_test.py)
memory.the leak: ggml-alloc freed and reallocated the target's 3352 MiB compute buffer whenever a graph needed a few MiB more than the reserved one (3352 -> 3357 -> 3362 -> 3367 MiB); ROCm on Windows keeps a freed buffer's commit, and a request a few MiB larger never reuses it, so each reallocation added ~3.4 GB for the rest of the process
memory.the fix: compute buffers get 3% + 16 MiB of headroom: no reallocation after the reserve. The four-conversation run peaks at 83.7 GB with 6.9 GB of commit to spare; 0.1.10 peaked at 90.4 GB with 0.18 GB to spare - the "bad allocation" seen once in ~16 multi-slot runs
memory.device memory: four slots, 262144 cells: weights 61.2 GiB + the draft's 2.1, KV pool 8.1 (target K/V 6.0, indexer 0.75, block keys 0.75, draft 0.63 - 32.5 KiB a cell), recurrent state 1.8, compute buffers 3.35 + 1.49: 78.3 GiB of the 96 GiB carve

runtime.finding: a build run from src/llama.cpp/build/bin or bin/hip-rocm101 has no ROCm DLLs beside it and Windows searches System32 before PATH, so it loaded the display driver's amdhip64_7.dll and amd_comgr_3.dll, while hipBLAS, rocBLAS and hipBLASLt came from the SDK. The bundle carries the SDK's HIP runtime
runtime.same binaries, two layouts: the release build on the probe above: 29.50 against 37.77 tok/s with MTP (acceptance 147 of 304 against 170 of 240), 44.78 against 43.47 ms/token without; the first token's top-3 already differ (-0.683 against -0.833) and the text from token 9. On the 18.6K equivalence prompt the first token's top logprob is -0.035 against -0.049 at ubatch 8192 (the text differs from token 20) and -0.047 against -0.520 at ubatch 4096. Every earlier comparison had both sides in the build layout
runtime.the fix: bootstrap.py --build copies the SDK's copies of the DLLs System32 would shadow (found by walking ggml-hip's imports) beside the build; the manager tells a bundle by hipblas.dll now. With them the build layout reproduces the bundle bitwise

open.total pool size: the pool is the context (262144 cells) however many slots there are; llama.cpp already separates the two (-c with --kv-unified-per-slot), so a larger pool for several long conversations is a manager setting - bounded by the carve and, before that, the commit limit
